nodes.name: How AI is Changing SEO
nodes.description: AI systems are changing how people find information, moving some search behavior away from typing keywords into a search bar and toward asking questions directly to a chat interface. This shift means content now needs to work for two audiences: traditional search crawlers and AI systems that retrieve and summarize information. The technical mechanics behind this shift, such as how AI models process and retrieve text, are covered in more depth in the AI Engineer roadmap.

nodes.name: Citation Resources
nodes.description: Citation sources are the specific websites and platforms that AI systems most frequently pull from and cite when generating answers, such as community forums, encyclopedic sites, and video platforms. Understanding which sources get cited most often helps prioritize where a brand should have a genuine, active presence.

nodes.name: Preferred Sources
nodes.description: Preferred sources are the specific websites and publications that a given AI system consistently favors when choosing what to cite, often shaped by factors like established authority, structured content, or crawl accessibility. Identifying which sources an AI system prefers within a given topic helps inform where content or PR efforts might be most effective.

nodes.name: Agentic Search
nodes.description: Agentic search is when an AI system does not just answer a question, but takes actions on a user's behalf, such as browsing multiple pages, comparing options, or completing a task like booking or purchasing. It represents a shift from search as information retrieval toward search as a component of autonomous task completion.

nodes.name: How Agents Browse
nodes.description: This covers the technical process by which an AI agent navigates websites autonomously, including how it reads page content, follows links, and interprets forms or buttons to complete a task, generally without a human directing each individual step.

nodes.name: MCP & Structured Access
nodes.description: MCP, or Model Context Protocol, is a standard that lets AI systems connect to external tools and data sources in a structured, predictable way, rather than only reading unstructured web pages. Structured access through protocols like this can give AI agents more reliable, direct access to a website's data than scraping its rendered HTML.

nodes.name: Link Building
nodes.description: Link building is the practice of getting other websites to link to your own. Search engines treat links from other sites as a signal of trust and authority, so a page with many relevant, high-quality links pointing to it is generally treated as more credible than one with none.

nodes.name: Digital PR
nodes.description: Digital PR is the practice of earning media coverage and links from real publications by pitching journalists newsworthy stories, data, or angles, rather than directly requesting a link.

nodes.name: Data-Driven PR
nodes.description: Data-driven PR is a specific digital PR tactic where a brand runs original research or a survey, then pitches journalists the resulting statistics as the basis for a story. It gives journalists something concrete and citable to write about, increasing the odds of coverage compared to a generic pitch.

nodes.name: Influencer Outreach
nodes.description: Influencer outreach is the practice of getting individual creators, bloggers, or influencers to mention, review, or link to a brand. It works similarly to digital PR but targets individual voices with their own audiences, rather than publications.

nodes.name: Entity Consistency
nodes.description: Entity consistency is how uniformly a brand or person's identity appears across the web, including directories, social profiles, and mentions that are not directly controlled by that brand. Search and AI systems use this consistency to confirm that scattered mentions across the internet all refer to the same real entity, rather than several unrelated ones.

nodes.name: Author & Org. Consistency
nodes.description: This is making sure the name, biography, and stated facts about an author or organization match wherever they appear, whether on the company's own site, a guest post, or a professional profile. Inconsistent details, such as different job titles or misspelled names, make it harder for a system to confirm it is looking at the same entity.

nodes.name: Directories & Databases
nodes.description: Directories and databases are external listings of a business or brand, such as industry directories or structured data sources. They act as independent confirmations of a brand's existence and details, beyond what the brand claims about itself on its own website.

nodes.name: Social Profiles
nodes.description: Social profiles are a brand or individual's presence on platforms like LinkedIn or X. They serve as another point of confirmation for a system trying to verify identity, and are often referenced when knowledge graphs cross-check who or what an entity actually is.

nodes.name: Unlinked Brand Mentions
nodes.description: An unlinked brand mention is when a brand name is referenced somewhere online without an accompanying clickable link back to its website. These mentions carry little weight in traditional link-based ranking, but they still count as evidence that a brand exists and is being discussed, which matters to entity-based and AI retrieval systems.

nodes.name: Community Presence
nodes.description: Community presence is a brand or individual's activity and reputation within online communities such as Reddit, Quora, and niche forums, where people ask questions and share opinions candidly. These communities are increasingly pulled from directly by AI systems when forming answers, making genuine presence there valuable beyond traditional SEO value.

nodes.name: Niche Forums
nodes.description: Niche forums are smaller, topic-specific online communities focused on a particular industry, hobby, or interest, as opposed to large general platforms. They often contain highly specific, candid discussion that both search and AI systems draw on when answering detailed questions within that niche.

nodes.name: Local Search
nodes.description: Local search covers the baseline setup required to appear in local search results, before rankings can meaningfully improve. This includes claiming and completing a Google Business Profile, keeping business details consistent everywhere they appear, gathering citations from other sites, and building dedicated pages for each location or service area served.

nodes.name: International SEO
nodes.description: International SEO is the practice of optimizing a website to serve and rank well for audiences in multiple countries or languages, addressing how content, URLs, and targeting signals differ across markets.

nodes.name: Hreflang
nodes.description: Hreflang is an HTML attribute that tells search engines which language and regional version of a page to show to users based on their location and language settings. It prevents search engines from showing the wrong language version, or treating translated versions of the same page as duplicate content.

nodes.name: ccTLD, Subfolder, Subdomain
nodes.description: A ccTLD is a country-specific domain ending, like .de for Germany, giving the strongest signal of geographic targeting but requiring separate domains for each market. A subfolder keeps international content under one main domain, such as [example.com/de/](http://example.com/de/), while a subdomain places it on a separate address like [de.example.com](http://de.example.com). Each approach involves different tradeoffs between geographic targeting strength and shared domain authority.

nodes.name: Geo-Targeting & Localization
nodes.description: Geo-targeting is signaling to search engines which country or region a page is intended for, while localization is adapting the page itself for that audience, including language, currency, spelling, and units. Signals such as hreflang annotations, a country-specific domain or URL structure, and genuinely localized content help search engines serve the right version of a page to the right users.

nodes.name: Video SEO
nodes.description: Video SEO is the practice of optimizing video content and its surrounding metadata so it can be found through search, both on platforms like YouTube and within traditional search engine results.

nodes.name: E-commerce SEO
nodes.description: Ecommerce SEO is the practice of optimizing an online store's product and category pages so they rank well in search, addressing challenges specific to retail sites like large product catalogs and complex filtering systems.

nodes.name: News & Discovery SEO
nodes.description: News and Discovery SEO is about earning visibility in Google surfaces that recommend content without a typed query, such as Top Stories, Google News, and the Discover feed. These surfaces favor fresh, original, well-sourced content with clear authorship and publish dates, high-quality images, and headlines that describe the story accurately rather than relying on clickbait.

nodes.name: Google Discover
nodes.description: Google Discover is a personalized content feed shown on mobile devices, surfacing articles based on a user's interests rather than a specific search query. Appearing in Discover depends on factors like content quality and image optimization, but there is no way to directly target it the way you can target a specific keyword.

nodes.name: Google Search Console
nodes.description: Google Search Console is a free tool from Google that shows exactly how a website performs in Google's own search results, including which queries it appears for, click-through rates, indexing errors, and manual penalties.

nodes.name: GSC API & BigQuery Export
nodes.description: The Google Search Console API allows programmatic access to search performance data, rather than only viewing it through the web interface. The BigQuery export sends this data automatically into Google's BigQuery platform, enabling larger scale analysis and longer data retention than Search Console's standard interface allows.

nodes.name: Visibility Metrics
nodes.description: Visibility metrics are the core numbers used to describe how visible a website is in traditional search, including how often it shows up, how often people click, where it ranks on average,

nodes.name: Impressions, Clicks & CTR
nodes.description: Impressions are how often a page appears in search results for a query, whether or not anyone clicks it. Clicks are how many people actually click through. CTR, or click-through rate, is the percentage of impressions that turn into clicks, and a low CTR relative to ranking position can signal that a title or description is not compelling enough.

nodes.name: Position & Share of Search
nodes.description: Average position is where a page typically ranks for a given query. Share of search measures what percentage of all search interest in a category or topic a brand is actually capturing, which gives a broader view of visibility than tracking individual keyword rankings alone.

nodes.name: Branded vs Non-Branded
nodes.description: Branded queries are searches that include a company's name, such as "Nike running shoes," while non-branded queries are generic searches without it, such as "best running shoes." Tracking the split between the two shows whether traffic is coming mostly from people who already know the brand or from people discovering it for the first time.

nodes.name: Query & Topic Coverage
nodes.description: Query coverage is how many relevant search queries a site actually appears for, out of all the queries related to its topic. Topic coverage looks at this at a broader level, checking whether a site comprehensively addresses a subject or only touches a small part of it.

nodes.name: Rank Tracking
nodes.description: Rank tracking is the practice of monitoring where a website ranks for specific target keywords over time, using dedicated tools that check search results regularly.

nodes.name: Semrush
nodes.description: Semrush is an all-in-one marketing software suite that provides tools for keyword research, competitor analysis, and position tracking. It allows users to monitor their search engine rankings across various devices and locations, offering detailed data on visibility trends and performance changes over time.

nodes.name: AccuRanker
nodes.description: AccuRanker is a rank tracking tool built specifically for speed and accuracy at scale, commonly used by agencies and larger sites that need to track rankings for a large number of keywords.

nodes.name: Traffic Analysis
nodes.description: Traffic analysis is the practice of understanding what visitors actually do once they land on a website, including where they came from, which pages they visit, and how they interact with the page.

nodes.name: Google Analytics
nodes.description: Google Analytics is a free web analytics platform that tracks website traffic, including where visitors come from, which pages they view, and whether they complete meaningful actions like purchases or sign-ups.

nodes.name: Microsoft Clarity
nodes.description: Microsoft Clarity is a free analytics tool that provides heatmaps and session recordings, showing how visitors actually move through and interact with a page, rather than just reporting traffic numbers.

nodes.name: Google Data Studio
nodes.description: Google Data Studio, now known as Looker Studio, is a free tool for building custom dashboards and reports by pulling data from sources like Google Analytics and Search Console into a single visual interface.

nodes.name: LLM Referral Traffic
nodes.description: LLM referral traffic is website visits that originate specifically from a link clicked inside an AI chat assistant's response, such as a source cited by ChatGPT or Perplexity. Tracking it separately from other referral traffic shows how much real, measurable value AI visibility is actually generating.

nodes.name: Zero-Click Attribution
nodes.description: Zero-click attribution is the practice of measuring the value of searches where a user gets their answer directly on the results page, or from an AI-generated response, without ever clicking through to a website. These searches used to be largely invisible to standard analytics, even though they still represent real brand exposure.

nodes.name: Domain Authority
nodes.description: Domain Authority is a score developed by Moz that estimates how likely an entire website is to rank in search results, based largely on the quantity and quality of links pointing to it. It is measured on a relative scale and is most useful for comparing one site against another, rather than as an absolute number.

nodes.name: Page Authority
nodes.description: Page Authority is a Moz metric similar to Domain Authority, but measured for a single page instead of an entire website. It estimates how likely that specific page is to rank well, based on the links pointing directly to it.

nodes.name: Trust Flow
nodes.description: Trust Flow is a metric from Majestic that estimates how trustworthy a website is, based on the quality of sites linking to it rather than just the quantity. A page linked to by a small number of highly trusted sites can score higher than one linked to by many low-quality sites.

nodes.name: Citation Flow
nodes.description: Citation Flow is a metric from Majestic that estimates the raw link popularity of a website, based on how many sites link to it regardless of their quality. It is typically compared alongside Trust Flow, since a large gap between the two can indicate a site has many low-quality links.

nodes.name: Nofollow, Sponsored, UGC
nodes.description: The nofollow attribute tells search engines not to pass ranking credit through a link. The sponsored attribute specifically marks a link as paid or part of an advertising arrangement. The UGC, or user-generated content, attribute marks links found in content like comments or forum posts, which a site owner did not personally place or endorse.

nodes.name: Ahrefs
nodes.description: Ahrefs is an all-in-one software suite that provides data on backlinks, keyword rankings, and website performance. It works by crawling the web to map out how pages connect to one another, allowing users to analyze their own site’s link profile or research the backlink strategies of competitors. The platform offers a variety of tools to identify broken links, monitor new link acquisition, and discover opportunities for outreach to improve overall site visibility.

nodes.name: BuzzStream
nodes.description: BuzzStream is an outreach and relationship management tool used in link building and digital PR, helping practitioners track contacts, send pitches, and manage ongoing outreach campaigns at scale.

nodes.name: Majestic
nodes.description: Majestic is a backlink analysis tool best known for producing the Trust Flow and Citation Flow metrics, which estimate the quality and quantity of links pointing to a website.

nodes.name: Pitchbox
nodes.description: Pitchbox is an outreach automation platform used for link building and digital PR, helping teams find contacts, send templated pitches, and manage follow-ups across large outreach campaigns.

nodes.name: Ahrefs Brand Radar
nodes.description: Ahrefs Brand Radar is a feature that tracks how often and how prominently a brand appears within AI-generated answers, extending Ahrefs' existing tracking capabilities from traditional search into AI visibility.

nodes.name: AI Visibility Measurement
nodes.description: AI visibility measurement is the set of metrics used to track how visible a brand is inside AI-generated answers, covering how often it appears across a set of representative prompts, how often and how prominently it gets cited, how it compares to competitors, and whether it is associated with positive or neutral sentiment.

nodes.name: Prompt Coverage & Mention
nodes.description: Prompt coverage measures how often a brand appears across a representative set of prompts within its category, when tested against AI systems. Mention rate is the frequency of those appearances, whether or not the brand is directly cited as a source.

nodes.name: Citation Rate & Position
nodes.description: Citation rate is how often an AI system cites a particular source when generating an answer. Citation position refers to how prominently that source appears within the citations, since being the first source listed generally carries more visibility and credibility than being buried further down.

nodes.name: Competitive Answer Share
nodes.description: Competitive answer share measures a brand's presence in AI-generated answers relative to its competitors, across the same set of prompts. It shows whether a brand is winning, losing, or roughly matching its competitors for visibility inside AI systems.

nodes.name: Entity & Sentiment
nodes.description: This tracks whether an AI system correctly associates a brand with the right topics and entities, and whether that association carries positive, neutral, or negative sentiment. A brand can be frequently mentioned by an AI system while still being associated with the wrong context or an unfavorable tone.

nodes.name: Profound
nodes.description: Profound is a platform built specifically to track how often and how favorably a brand appears within AI-generated answers across different AI systems.

nodes.name: Otterly
nodes.description: Otterly is a tool that monitors brand visibility and citations within AI search and chat platforms, tracking how often a brand appears and in what context.

nodes.name: Peec
nodes.description: Peec is a platform for tracking a brand's presence and share of voice within AI-generated answers, comparing performance against competitors across a defined set of prompts.

nodes.name: GEO & SEO Testing
nodes.description: This is the practice of running structured experiments to check whether a change actually improved visibility, rather than assuming it did. It includes testing content or schema changes, comparing AI-generated answers before and after a change, and benchmarking performance against competitors.

nodes.name: Content & Schema A/B Tests
nodes.description: This is testing two versions of a page's content or structured data against each other to see which one performs better in search or AI visibility, rather than assuming a change is an improvement without checking.

nodes.name: Before/After Prompt Tests
nodes.description: This means running the same set of AI prompts before and after making a change to a website, then comparing the answers to see whether the change actually affected how AI systems describe or cite the brand.

nodes.name: Competitor Benchmarking
nodes.description: Competitor benchmarking is the practice of comparing a website's search and AI visibility performance directly against competitors, rather than only tracking its own metrics in isolation. It gives context for whether a given number is actually good or bad within the competitive landscape.

nodes.name: SEO Audits
nodes.description: An SEO audit is a structured review of a website's technical health, content quality, and backlink profile, identifying issues and opportunities across all of these areas at once. It is typically the first step in diagnosing why a site is underperforming or in establishing a baseline before starting new work.
